【Good Points】
- Open 365 days a year.
- Thorough examinations.
- Large staff (2-3 doctors and 4-5 nurses on duty at all times).
- Doctors and nurses are generally friendly and polite.

【Bad Points】
- Most doctors work at other branches of the group, only being present 2-3 days a week.
- Therefore, seeing the same doctor limits appointment days.
- Patient information isn't properly shared when seeing different doctors.
- Occasionally, there are miscommunications or misunderstandings between doctors, nurses, and pet owners.
- Consultation fees are on the higher side, possibly due to the various tests and treatments performed.
- No restrooms. The building is old and cramped.
- Only one parking space available. There are only metered parking (60 minutes) nearby; no coin-operated parking.

【Areas for Improvement】
- Eliminate doctors working at other branches: Being able to always see a trusted doctor provides greater peace of mind.

- Electronic medical record system: If doctors' rotation schedules are unavoidable, at the very least, an electronic medical record system should be implemented to ensure thorough information sharing.

- Building relocation/renovation: While the aging infrastructure, lack of toilets and parking, and other issues are problematic, the back office space is extremely cramped.

Management should create a comfortable and efficient working environment for doctors and nurses.

When I went to visit, everyone seemed busy, and I was hesitant to speak to them because I wasn't sure if it was okay to approach them. That's when Nurse Narita (apologies if I got the name wrong) spoke to me. She answered all my questions with a smile and in a polite manner, and I felt that she truly cared for my child. I feel confident entrusting my child to this hospital. She was wearing a new nurse's badge, so I hope she does well from now on. Thank you for everything.

The veterinarian is very kind and attentive, and listens carefully to what you have to say, making it a reassuring animal hospital to have your pet examined. The explanations were thorough, the spaying surgery was successful, and the post-operative recovery was good. I feel that the veterinarian is trustworthy.

On the other hand, even with an appointment, the waiting time is often long, and I would appreciate it if this could be improved.

Also, I felt the cost was quite high. In my case, for my dog's spaying surgery, the pre-operative examination was about 20,000 yen, the abdominal surgery was 77,000 yen, the extraction of one deciduous tooth was 3,300 yen, and including the Elizabethan collar and medication costs, the total cost was about 130,000 yen. Of course, the pricing varies from hospital to hospital, but compared to what I've heard from friends and other hospitals, I got the impression that it was higher than average. Those planning to visit this hospital should check the estimated costs beforehand.
Ms. Shizuka and the rest of the staff all communicate with you in a two-way manner, so you can entrust your pet to them with peace of mind.
The receptionists and doctors are very kind and it's a very relaxing space!

I use this clinic whenever something comes up.

The veterinarians are always kind and helpful, and I'm always grateful for their assistance.

The wait is unbearable. You typically wait about an hour before even seeing your pet. Then, they take your pet for tests, and it takes another 60 minutes for the results. After hearing the results, you have to wait another 30-60 minutes before you can pay.

And yet, the waiting room is small, and there's no toilet for pet owners.

It seems like they've opened too many branches and are understaffed.

If they're making enough money to open branches, they should improve the quality of each one.
They were very helpful and polite.
This was my first visit, but the doctors and reception staff were all very kind and explained everything thoroughly. I'm glad I went. I plan to use this clinic again as my regular local hospital.

My dog's paw pads were red, so I took him to the vet. I was told, "Let's see how it goes with a little anti-itch cream," but I ended up buying a 30-day supply of anti-itch cream, which cost tens of thousands of yen. I think it's dishonest to prescribe so much medication without prior explanation. I have absolutely no trust in them.
They were able to find a condition that other clinics couldn't detect. There are many young doctors, but they explain things thoroughly and are trustworthy.
